    18→// Layer Name Normalization
    19→
    20→/// Normalize a layer name by stripping `{page_id}/` prefix if present
    21→///
    22→/// **Context**: Lua apps and wire protocol use prefixed names (`{page_id}/messages`)
    23→/// but Scribe stores layers with bare names (`messages`). This strips the prefix
    24→/// at the Scribe boundary so all internal lookups use consistent bare names.
    25→pub fn normalize_layer_name(name: &str, page_id: &str) -> String {
    26→    let prefix = format!("{}/", page_id);
    27→    if let Some(bare) = name.strip_prefix(&prefix) {
    28→        bare.to_string()
    29→    } else {
    30→        name.to_string()
    31→    }
    32→}

    34→// Sync Configuration
    35→
    36→/// Sync mode derived from permit capabilities
    37→///
    38→/// **Design**: Capability-based, not role-based
    39→/// - Mode is derived from permit's sync configuration
    40→/// - No hardcoded role names in decision logic
    41→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    42→pub enum SyncMode {
    43→    /// Sync to a specific source node (users sync to their node)
    44→    ToSource,
    45→    /// Broadcast to all authorized peers (node mode)
    46→    Broadcast,
    47→}
    48→
    49→impl Default for SyncMode {
    50→    fn default() -> Self {
    51→        SyncMode::Broadcast
    52→    }
    53→}
    54→
    55→/// Sync configuration derived from permit
    56→///
    57→/// **Context**: Determines how this Scribe syncs based on permit capabilities
    58→/// - ToSource: Sync to a specific source node (owner/viewer/customer)
    59→/// - Broadcast: Broadcast to all authorized peers (node)
    60→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    61→pub struct SyncConfig {
    62→    /// Sync mode derived from permit (capability-based)
    63→    pub mode: SyncMode,
    64→    /// For ToSource: node_id to sync to
    65→    /// For Broadcast: None (uses list_authorized_users callback)
    66→    pub sync_target: Option<String>,
    67→}

    69→// Subscriber Types
    70→
    71→/// Information about a subscribed peer
    72→///
    73→/// **Design**: Stores the parsed permit directly instead of extracted fields.
    74→/// All access checks delegate to gurkha::Permit methods, ensuring consistency.
    75→pub struct SubscriberInfo {
    76→    /// Parsed page permit for all access checks (static layers)
    77→    /// Stores the full permit so we can use its methods directly
    78→    pub permit: gurkha::Permit,
    79→    /// Layer permits (dynamic layers) — additive, one per dynamic layer
    80→    pub layer_permits: Vec<gurkha::Permit>,
    81→    /// Subscriber's DID (for pattern expansion with {aud})
    82→    /// Extracted from permit audience and normalized to DID format
    83→    pub subscriber_did: String,
    84→    /// Whether this subscriber is visible (from permit presence config)
    85→    /// Visible peers have their entry written to the presence layer
    86→    pub is_visible: bool,
    87→    /// Whether this subscriber can see others' presence
    88→    /// Gates whether the presence layer is synced to this peer
    89→    pub can_see_others: bool,
    90→    /// Display name for this subscriber (from permit presence config)
    91→    pub display_name: Option<String>,
    92→    /// Channel to send CRDT broadcasts
    93→    pub broadcast_tx: mpsc::Sender<BroadcastPayload>,
    94→    /// Channel to send ephemeral broadcasts (cursor, typing)
    95→    /// PeerActor creates this, spawns listener that sends datagrams
    96→    pub ephemeral_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<EphemeralOutbound>>,
    97→    /// Their last known state vectors (layer_name → version_vector)
    98→    pub vectors: HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
    99→}
   100→
   101→impl SubscriberInfo {
   102→    /// Check if subscriber can receive updates for layer (two-tier)
   103→    ///
   104→    /// **Context**: Used during broadcast/reconciliation to check read permission
   105→    /// **Two-tier**: Checks page permit (static layers) then layer permits (dynamic layers)
   106→    pub fn can_receive_layer(&self, layer_name: &str, page_id: &str) -> bool {
   107→        // Block presence layer for peers who can't see others
   108→        if (layer_name == "presence" || layer_name.ends_with("/presence")) && !self.can_see_others {
   109→            return false;
   110→        }
   111→        // Check if layer is in no_incoming_updates (sync facts)
   112→        if self.permit.sync_facts().no_incoming_updates.contains(&layer_name.to_string()) {
   113→            return false;
   114→        }
   115→        // Two-tier check: page permit OR any layer permit
   116→        gurkha::can_access_with_layer_permits(
   117→            &self.permit, &self.layer_permits,
   118→            layer_name, page_id, &self.subscriber_did, "read",
   119→        )
   120→    }
   121→
   122→    /// Check if subscriber can write to layer (two-tier)
   123→    ///
   124→    /// **Context**: Used during incoming update validation
   125→    /// **Two-tier**: Checks page permit then layer permits
   126→    pub fn can_write_layer(&self, layer_name: &str, page_id: &str) -> bool {
   127→        gurkha::can_access_with_layer_permits(
   128→            &self.permit, &self.layer_permits,
   129→            layer_name, page_id, &self.subscriber_did, "write",
   130→        )
   131→    }
   132→
   133→    /// Add a layer permit (additive, no replacement)
   134→    ///
   135→    /// **Context**: Node issued a new layer permit for a dynamic layer
   136→    pub fn add_layer_permit(&mut self, permit: gurkha::Permit) {
   137→        self.layer_permits.push(permit);
   138→    }
   139→}

   200→    pub validation_handle: Option<crate::validation_handle::ValidationHandle>,
   201→
   202→    /// Parsed permit - provides should_sync_layer, can_write_layer etc.
   203→    /// Uses gurkha::Permit directly with page_id/did passed to methods

   205→    /// Our DID (for pattern expansion with {aud})
   206→    pub our_did: String,
   207→
   208→    /// Shutdown sender for node script tick loop (if running)
   209→    /// **Context**: Set when is_node=true and entry_node found in manifest

   214→/// Arguments for spawning Scribe
   215→pub struct ScribeArgs {
   216→    pub page_id: String,
   217→    pub layers: HashMap<String, Layer>,
   218→
   219→    /// Layer persistence (saves layer snapshots)
   220→    pub layer_storage: LayerStorageRef,
   221→    /// Peer vector persistence (saves/loads peer state vectors)
   222→    pub vector_storage: PeerVectorStorageRef,
   223→    /// Peer resolver (node mode only) - lists authorized users, loads permits
   224→    pub peer_resolver: Option<PeerResolverRef>,
   225→    /// Permit issuer (node mode only) - issues layer permits for dynamic layers
   226→    pub permit_issuer: Option<PermitIssuerRef>,
   227→
   228→    /// Optional: Sync configuration derived from permit (relationship + sync_target)
   229→    /// - Owner: sync to sovereign node
   230→    /// - Node: broadcast only (no outbound sync)
   231→    /// - Viewer: sync to source node
   232→    pub sync_config: Option<SyncConfig>,
   233→    /// Channel to emit sync events (EnsureSync) - consumed by Coordinator
   234→    pub sync_event_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<SyncEvent>>,
   235→    /// Validation handle (for kunki node mode validation)
   236→    /// If provided, Scribe delegates validation to external ValidationService
   237→    pub validation_handle: Option<crate::validation_handle::ValidationHandle>,
   238→    /// Our permit for this page (local write authorization)
   239→    /// Used to check if we can write to a layer before committing
   240→    pub our_permit: Option<String>,
   241→    /// Our DID (for pattern expansion and validation)
   242→    pub our_did: String,
   243→    /// Our username (for node script permit bindings)
   244→    pub our_username: String,
   245→    /// Whether this Scribe runs on a node (enables derivation engine and node scripts)
   246→    pub is_node: bool,
   247→    // Note: ephemeral_broadcast_tx removed - outbound ephemeral now goes directly via
   248→    // SubscriberInfo.ephemeral_tx (Scribe → PeerActor channels)
   249→}
   250→
   251→impl ScribeState {
   252→    /// Check if a layer should sync based on permit configuration
   253→    ///
   254→    /// **Context**: Used to filter out local-only layers (sync: false) before broadcasting
   255→    /// **Returns**: true if layer should sync, false if local-only
   256→    pub fn should_sync_layer(&self, layer_name: &str) -> bool {
   257→        self.our_permit
   258→            .as_ref()
   259→            .map(|permit| permit.should_sync_layer(layer_name, &self.page_id, &self.our_did))
   260→            .unwrap_or(true)  // No permit means sync everything
   261→    }
   262→
   263→    /// Check if we can write to a layer
   264→    pub fn can_write_layer(&self, layer_name: &str) -> bool {
   265→        self.our_permit
   266→            .as_ref()
   267→            .map(|permit| permit.can_write_layer(layer_name, &self.page_id, &self.our_did))
   268→            .unwrap_or(true)  // No permit means full access
   269→    }
   270→}

1→//! Scribe message types
     2→//!
     3→//! Contains both the actor messages (ScribeMessage) and shared types
     4→//! (BroadcastPayload, PageUpdate, etc.)

     6→use std::collections::HashMap;
     7→use std::path::PathBuf;
     8→
     9→use ractor::RpcReplyPort;
    10→use tokio::sync::mpsc;
    11→use serde::{Serialize, Deserialize};
    12→
    13→use domains::{QuerySpec, QueryDelta, QueryResult, JsonOp};
    14→use crate::Result;
    15→
    16→/// Payload sent to PeerActor for broadcast (3-step sync protocol)
    17→///
    18→/// **Context**: Scribe sends this to PeerActor, who then sends SyncOffer to peer
    19→/// **state_vector**: Our state vector after this update (for 3-step protocol)
    20→/// **layer_type**: Protocol routing hint (App=snapshot, Data=incremental, Static=blob)
    21→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    22→pub struct BroadcastPayload {
    23→    pub page_id: String,
    24→    pub layer_name: String,
    25→    pub update: Vec<u8>,
    26→    /// Our state vector for this layer (for SyncOffer message)
    27→    pub state_vector: Vec<u8>,
    28→    /// Layer type for protocol routing
    29→    pub layer_type: domains::LayerType,
    30→}
    31→
    32→/// Ephemeral broadcast payload (generic)
    33→///
    34→/// **Context**: Scribe sends this to Butler/Courier for datagram broadcast
    35→/// **Transport**: Unreliable QUIC datagram (fire-and-forget, lowest latency)
    36→/// **Design**: Generic payload - app defines format; protocol routes by page_id
    37→#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
    38→pub struct EphemeralBroadcast {
    39→    /// Page ID for routing
    40→    pub page_id: String,
    41→    /// Opaque payload - app defines format (JSON with type/x/y, etc.)
    42→    pub payload: Vec<u8>,
    43→}
    44→
    45→/// Outbound ephemeral data (Scribe → PeerActor via channel)
    46→///
    47→/// **Context**: Same pattern as BroadcastPayload for CRDT data
    48→/// **Flow**: Scribe broadcasts ephemeral to all subscriber channels,
    49→///           PeerActor listener receives and sends datagram to peer
    50→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    51→pub struct EphemeralOutbound {
    52→    /// Page ID for routing (used in datagram)
    53→    pub page_id: String,
    54→    /// Opaque payload - app defines format (JSON with type/x/y, etc.)
    55→    pub payload: Vec<u8>,
    56→}
    57→
    58→/// Delta operations for different Loro container types
    59→///
    60→/// **Context**: Represents incremental changes to CRDT containers
    61→/// **Usage**: Lua apps can apply deltas for efficient UI updates (preserve scroll, animations)
    62→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    63→#[serde(tag = "type")]
    64→pub enum LoroDelta {
    65→    /// List delta: sequence of Retain/Insert/Delete operations
    66→    List { ops: Vec<ListOp> },
    67→
    68→    /// Map delta: updated keys
    69→    Map { updated: HashMap<String, Option<serde_json::Value>> },
    70→
    71→    /// Text delta (for future rich text support)
    72→    Text { ops: Vec<TextOp> },
    73→}
    74→
    75→/// List delta operations (applied sequentially)
    76→///
    77→/// **Context**: Represents changes to a Loro list container
    78→/// **Example**: [Retain(3), Insert([msg4]), Delete(1)] means "skip 3 items, insert msg4, delete 1 item"
    79→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    80→#[serde(tag = "op")]
    81→pub enum ListOp {
    82→    /// Keep N items unchanged (advance cursor)
    83→    Retain { count: usize },
    84→
    85→    /// Insert values at current position
    86→    Insert { values: Vec<serde_json::Value> },
    87→
    88→    /// Delete N items at current position
    89→    Delete { count: usize },
    90→}
    91→
    92→/// Text delta operations (for rich text editing)
    93→///
    94→/// **Context**: Represents changes to a Loro text container
    95→/// **Note**: Deferred for now - will implement when we need rich text editing
    96→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    97→#[serde(tag = "op")]
    98→pub enum TextOp {
    99→    /// Keep N characters unchanged
   100→    Retain { count: usize },
   101→
   102→    /// Insert text at current position
   103→    Insert { text: String },
   104→
   105→    /// Delete N characters at current position
   106→    Delete { count: usize },
   107→}

   109→// Unified Page Update Channel (Replaces PageEvent + EphemeralEvent + QueryDelta)
   110→
   111→/// Unified update enum for all page events
   112→///
   113→/// **Context**: Single channel replaces 3 separate broadcast types
   114→/// **Benefits**: 3 listener tasks → 1, unified fan-out logic
   115→/// **Consumers**: UI/Lua callbacks, Broadcast to peers, Derivation engine
   116→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   117→pub enum PageUpdate {
   118→    /// Layer data changed (local edit or remote sync)
   119→    LayerChanged {
   120→        layer: String,
   121→        from_peer: Option<(String, String)>,  // (did, device_id)
   122→        /// Structured operations extracted from the update (same format as validation)
   123→        /// Enables surgical UI updates - Lua can process individual ops
   124→        ops: Option<Vec<JsonOp>>,
   125→        delta: Option<LoroDelta>,
   126→        state_vector: Vec<u8>,
   127→        /// Full layer state as JSON — None when delta is available (avoids O(N) serialization)
   128→        /// Some for initial load, wildcard bindings, or fallback scenarios
   129→        full_data: Option<serde_json::Value>,
   130→        /// True if this is a newly created layer (first time seeing it)
   131→        created: bool,
   132→    },
   133→
   134→    /// Ephemeral data from remote peer (cursor, typing, etc.)
   135→    Ephemeral {
   136→        user_did: String,
   137→        device_id: String,
   138→        payload: Vec<u8>,
   139→    },
   140→
   141→    /// Query result changed
   142→    QueryUpdated {
   143→        query_id: String,
   144→        delta: QueryDelta,
   145→    },
   146→
   147→    /// Peer subscribed to this page
   148→    PeerSubscribed {
   149→        did: String,
   150→        /// Username if presence.share_username is true in their permit
   151→        username: Option<String>,
   152→    },
   153→
   154→    /// Peer unsubscribed from this page
   155→    PeerUnsubscribed {
   156→        did: String,
   157→    },
   158→
   159→    /// Structured ephemeral received (permission-validated)
   160→    ///
   161→    /// **Context**: Ephemeral with func name, validated against permit
   162→    StructuredEphemeral {
   163→        from_did: String,
   164→        func: String,
   165→        args: serde_json::Value,
   166→    },
   167→}
   168→
   169→/// Type alias for unified page update channel
   170→pub type PageUpdateTx = mpsc::Sender<PageUpdate>;
   171→
   172→/// Events emitted for sync coordination (consumed by Coordinator)
   173→///
   174→/// **Context**: Scribe emits these when it needs to sync with a user.
   175→/// NOTE: Scribe only knows user_did. Coordinator handles everything else:
   176→/// - Device resolution
   177→/// - Connection establishment
   178→/// - Subscription (PeerActor discovers active Scribes on connect)
   179→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   180→pub enum SyncEvent {
   181→    /// Ensure this user is synced (connected + subscribed to active Scribes)
   182→    EnsureSync { user_did: String },
   183→
   184→    /// Node detected a new dynamic layer — permits already created by layer_unit
   185→    ///
   186→    /// **Context**: Scribe detected a dynamic layer (via schema match) and used
   187→    /// PermitIssuer to create ready-to-send permits. Coordinator just distributes.
   188→    NewDynamicLayer {
   189→        page_id: String,
   190→        layer_name: String,
   191→        /// Ready-to-send permits: (recipient_did, layer_permit_token)
   192→        permits: Vec<(String, String)>,
   193→    },
   194→
   195→    /// Layer access changed — new permits need distribution
   196→    ///
   197→    /// **Context**: Scribe added a participant and issued permits for connected peers
   198→    LayerAccessChanged {
   199→        page_id: String,
   200→        layer_name: String,
   201→        /// Ready-to-send permits: (recipient_did, layer_permit_token)
   202→        permits: Vec<(String, String)>,
   203→    },
   204→}

   206→// ScribeMessage - Actor Messages for Scribe
   207→
   208→/// Messages received by Scribe actor
   209→#[derive(Debug)]
   210→pub enum ScribeMessage {
   211→    /// Peer subscription - PeerActor subscribes to receive layer updates
   212→    ///
   213→    /// **Context**: PeerActor connects for a page and wants sync updates
   214→    /// **We do**: Parse permit, extract layer permissions + sync policies, store subscriber
   215→    Subscribe {
   216→        user_did: String,
   217→        device_id: String,
   218→        /// Callback to send CRDT broadcasts to this peer
   219→        broadcast_tx: mpsc::Sender<BroadcastPayload>,
   220→        /// Callback to send ephemeral broadcasts to this peer (cursor, typing)
   221→        /// PeerActor creates this channel, spawns listener that sends datagrams
   222→        ephemeral_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<EphemeralOutbound>>,
   223→        /// Raw permit string - we parse to extract permissions
   224→        permit: String,
   225→    },
   226→
   227→    /// Peer unsubscription
   228→    Unsubscribe {
   229→        user_did: String,
   230→        device_id: String,
   231→    },
   232→
   233→    /// Apply layer update (from local UI or remote peer)
   234→    ///
   235→    /// **Context**: Local edit or remote sync push
   236→    /// **We do**: Permission check, CRDT merge, broadcast to subscribers
   237→    ApplyUpdate {
   238→        layer_name: String,
   239→        update: Vec<u8>,
   240→        /// None = local edit, Some = remote peer
   241→        from_peer: Option<(String, String)>,
   242→        /// Permit from SyncOffer (for peers not yet subscribed)
   243→        permit: Option<String>,
   244→    },
   245→
   246→    /// Apply layer update with result feedback (for SyncAccept control)
   247→    ///
   248→    /// **Context**: Remote sync push that needs success/failure feedback
   249→    /// **We do**: Permission check, CRDT merge, broadcast to subscribers, reply with result
   250→    ApplyUpdateWithResult {
   251→        layer_name: String,
   252→        update: Vec<u8>,
   253→        from_peer: Option<(String, String)>,
   254→        permit: Option<String>,
   255→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<std::result::Result<(), String>>,
   256→    },
   257→
   258→    /// Sync request - peer wants updates since their version
   259→    SyncRequest {
   260→        layer_name: String,
   261→        their_vector: Vec<u8>,
   262→        reply: RpcReplyPort<Result<Vec<u8>>>,
   263→    },
   264→
   265→    /// Export full snapshot (for initial sync or send_full_snapshot policy)
   266→    ExportSnapshot {
   267→        layer_name: String,
   268→        reply: RpcReplyPort<Result<Vec<u8>>>,
   269→    },
   270→
   271→    /// Get our state vector (for incremental sync)
   272→    GetStateVector {
   273→        layer_name: String,
   274→        reply: RpcReplyPort<Result<Vec<u8>>>,
   275→    },
   276→
   277→    /// Get updates since a given state vector (for resync after divergence)
   278→    ///
   279→    /// **Context**: SyncAccept showed divergence, sender needs full diff
   280→    /// **We do**: Export updates from our LoroDoc since their vector

## Summary

### What changed

**Core: `LayerUnit` now owns authorization** (`scribe/src/layer_unit/mod.rs`)
- Added `authorized_dids: Arc<RwLock<HashSet<String>>>` field
- Added `authorize_did()`, `revoke_did()`, `is_authorized()`, `authorized_dids()` methods

**New message** (`scribe/src/message.rs`)
- `ScribeMessage::AuthorizeLayerSubscriber { layer_name, subscriber_did }` — viewer sends this to local Scribe when receiving a layer permit from the node

**State** (`scribe/src/state.rs`)  
- Added `pending_layer_authorizations: HashMap<String, Vec<String>>` to `ScribeState`
- Removed `layer_permits` field from `SubscriberInfo`
- Removed `add_layer_permit()` method
- `can_receive_layer()` now checks page permit only (layer authorization is via `LayerUnit`)
- `can_write_layer()` simplified to page permit only

**Populate authorized_dids at 4 points:**
1. **Subscribe time** (`sync/subscription.rs`) — `authorize_subscriber_for_layers()` iterates all layers
2. **Layer creation** (`sync/apply.rs`) — `create_layer_from_peer()` checks existing subscribers + applies pending authorizations
3. **Dynamic layer from Lua** (`layer_unit/dynamic.rs`) — authorizes all current subscribers
4. **Permit issuance** (`sync/apply.rs`, `layer_unit/dynamic.rs`, `sync/subscription.rs`) — directly authorizes on `LayerUnit` instead of adding to `SubscriberInfo`

**Broadcast checks replaced** (3 files):
- `loro_observer.rs` — captures `authorized_dids` Arc, reads once per broadcast cycle
- `sync/broadcast.rs` — reads `authorized_dids` once before subscriber loop
- `sync/reconcile.rs` — reads per-layer authorization for divergence check

**Unsubscribe cleanup** (`sync/subscription.rs`) — revokes DID from all LayerUnits

**Viewer-side wiring** (`courier/src/peer_actor/consent.rs`) — `on_layer_permit()` sends `AuthorizeLayerSubscriber` to local Scribe

**Dead code removed:**
- `Permissions::can_receive()` from `permit.rs`

### Test results
- **18/18** scribe unit tests pass
- **55/55** gurkha tests pass
- **32/32** integration tests pass (including all 8 layer_sync tests)
- **16/16** app_test tests pass

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Custom Channel Capture Test — create channel, send messages, capture event flow.

Debugs the issue where only the owner can send messages in custom channels.
Captures all events during channel creation + message send from owner and viewer.

Usage:
    python e2e_tests/test_custom_channel.py
    python e2e_tests/test_custom_channel.py --keep
    python e2e_tests/test_custom_channel.py --capture-logs
"""

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent / "scripts"))

from osvauld.scenario import AppTestScenario

DEMOS_APP = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "sample_apps" / "osvauld-demos"

args = AppTestScenario.parse_args("Custom Channel Capture Test")

with AppTestScenario(
    name="custom_channel_test",
    app_path=str(DEMOS_APP),
    peers={
        "alice": {"role": "owner", "app": "Group Chat"},
        "bob": {"role": "viewer", "app": "Group Chat"},
        "carol": {"role": "viewer", "app": "Group Chat"},
    },
    **args,
) as s:
    alice = s.peer("alice")
    bob = s.peer("bob")
    carol = s.peer("carol")

    include_logs = "--capture-logs" in sys.argv

    # Start capture BEFORE the interesting operation
    print("[1/5] Starting event capture...")
    captures_dir = s.capture_start("custom_channel", include_logs=include_logs)
    print(f"  Capturing to {captures_dir}/")

    # Alice creates a custom channel (dynamic layer)
    print("[2/5] Alice creates custom channel 'project-x'...")
    alice.eval('create_channel("project-x")')
    time.sleep(2)

    # Alice sends a message in the new channel (create_channel auto-switches)
    print("[3/5] Alice sends message in 'project-x'...")
    alice.eval('send_message("Owner message in project-x")')
    time.sleep(2)

    # Bob switches to project-x and tries to send
    print("[4/5] Bob switches to 'project-x' and sends message...")
    bob.eval('switch_channel("project-x")')
    time.sleep(1)
    try:
        bob.eval('send_message("Bob message in project-x")')
        print("  Bob send_message returned OK")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  Bob send_message error: {e}")

    # Carol switches and tries to send
    print("  Carol switches to 'project-x' and sends message...")
    carol.eval('switch_channel("project-x")')
    time.sleep(1)
    try:
        carol.eval('send_message("Carol message in project-x")')
        print("  Carol send_message returned OK")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  Carol send_message error: {e}")

    # Wait for sync
    print("[5/5] Waiting 2s for sync...")
    time.sleep(2)

    # Check what each peer sees
    alice_count = alice.eval("return get_message_count()")
    bob_count = bob.eval("return get_message_count()")
    carol_count = carol.eval("return get_message_count()")
    print(f"\n  Message counts in project-x:")
    print(f"    Alice (owner):  {alice_count}")
    print(f"    Bob (viewer):   {bob_count}")
    print(f"    Carol (viewer): {carol_count}")

    # Stop capture and dump
    print("\n  Stopping capture and merging...")
    merged = s.capture_end("custom_channel", merge=True)

    if merged and merged.exists():
        line_count = sum(1 for _ in open(merged))
        print(f"  Captured {line_count} events -> {merged}")
        print(f"\n  Per-instance captures:")
        for name in ["node", "alice", "bob", "carol"]:
            f = captures_dir / f"custom_channel_{name}.jsonl"
            if f.exists():
                n = sum(1 for _ in open(f))
                print(f"    {name:8s}: {n} events")

        print(f"\n  Quick filters:")
        print(f"    grep 'sync_event' {merged}")
        print(f"    grep 'message_trace' {merged}")
        print(f"    grep 'page_update' {merged}")
        print(f"    grep 'LayerChanged' {merged}")
        print(f"    grep 'NewDynamicLayer' {merged}")
        print(f"    grep 'LayerAccessChanged' {merged}")
    else:
        print("  Warning: No capture data collected")

    print(f"\n{'=' * 60}")
    if alice_count >= 1:
        if bob_count >= 3 and carol_count >= 3:
            print("  [SUCCESS] All 3 messages synced to all peers")
        elif bob_count >= 1 or carol_count >= 1:
            print("  [PARTIAL] Owner message synced, viewer messages may be blocked")
            print("  Check the capture JSONL for permit/access issues")
        else:
            print("  [ISSUE] Owner message not reaching viewers")
            print("  Check the capture JSONL for layer sync issues")
    else:
        print("  [ISSUE] Even owner has no messages")
    print(f"{'=' * 60}")

# Observability: Event Capture System

## Overview

The event capture system records structured events from Courier and Scribe into JSONL files for debugging and AI analysis. It captures:

- **CourierEvents**: PeerAuthenticated, SpacePublished, ViewerSyncComplete, etc.
- **MessageTraces**: Protocol messages (Hello, Welcome, SyncOffer, etc.) with direction + node IDs
- **PageUpdates**: Layer changes, ephemeral data, peer subscriptions
- **SyncEvents**: EnsureSync, NewDynamicLayer, LayerAccessChanged
- **Tracing logs** (optional): All `tracing` log events from all crates

Capture is supported on both **kunki** (node) and **sthalam** (desktop shell) instances.

## JSONL Format

Each line is a self-contained JSON object with a `type` field and `ts` timestamp:

```json
{"type": "courier_event", "ts": "2026-02-11T15:30:00.123Z", "data": {"PeerAuthenticated": {"node_id": "abc...", "did": "did:key:...", "username": "alice"}}, "instance": "node"}
{"type": "message_trace", "ts": "2026-02-11T15:30:00.234Z", "direction": "Sent", "msg": "Hello", "node_id": "abc...", "peer_node_id": "def...", "instance": "owner"}
{"type": "page_update", "ts": "2026-02-11T15:30:00.345Z", "page_id": "pg_123", "data": {"LayerChanged": {"layer": "messages", ...}}, "instance": "node"}
{"type": "sync_event", "ts": "2026-02-11T15:30:00.456Z", "page_id": "pg_123", "data": "EnsureSync { user_did: \"did:key:...\" }", "instance": "node"}
{"type": "log", "ts": "2026-02-11T15:30:00.567Z", "level": "INFO", "target": "courier::coordinator", "msg": "Peer authenticated", "instance": "owner"}
```

## Usage from Python

### Single instance

```python
from osvauld.client import ControlClient

client = ControlClient("/tmp/test/node.sock")

# Start capturing (structured events only)
client.capture_start("/tmp/captures/node.jsonl")

# ... run operations ...

# Stop and flush
client.capture_end()
```

### With tracing logs

```python
client.capture_start("/tmp/captures/node.jsonl", include_logs=True)
```

### Multi-peer via AppTestScenario (E2E tests)

```python
from osvauld.scenario import AppTestScenario

DEMOS_APP = "sample_apps/osvauld-demos"

with AppTestScenario(
    name="my_test",
    app_path=DEMOS_APP,
    peers={
        "alice": {"role": "owner", "app": "Group Chat"},
        "bob": {"role": "viewer", "app": "Group Chat"},
    },
) as s:
    # Start capture on ALL instances (node + all peers)
    s.capture_start("my_label")

    # Run operations
    alice = s.peer("alice")
    alice.eval('create_channel("project-x")')
    alice.eval('send_message("Hello!")')
    time.sleep(2)

    # Stop and merge into sorted file
    merged = s.capture_end("my_label", merge=True)
    # → /tmp/my_test/captures/my_label_merged.jsonl
```

Output files:
```
/tmp/my_test/captures/
├── my_label_node.jsonl       # node events
├── my_label_alice.jsonl      # owner events
├── my_label_bob.jsonl        # viewer events
└── my_label_merged.jsonl     # all events sorted by timestamp
```

### Multi-peer via Scenario (low-level)

```python
from osvauld.scenario import Scenario

with Scenario(owner=1, node=1, viewer=1) as s:
    s.setup_owner(app_path="sample_apps/my-shop")
    s.connect_owner_to_node()

    s.capture_start("test_sync")

    # Run operations ...

    merged = s.capture_end("test_sync", merge=True)
    # → /tmp/osvauld_test/captures/test_sync_merged.jsonl
```

## E2E Test Scripts

| Script | What it tests |
|--------|--------------|
| `e2e_tests/test_chat.py` | Bidirectional message sync (3 users), captures events |
| `e2e_tests/test_custom_channel.py` | Dynamic channel creation + cross-peer sync, captures events |

```bash
# Run with capture
python e2e_tests/test_chat.py

# Also capture tracing logs (verbose)
python e2e_tests/test_custom_channel.py --capture-logs

# Keep tmux alive after test for debugging
python e2e_tests/test_custom_channel.py --keep
```

## Filtering Captures

```bash
# All sync events (EnsureSync, NewDynamicLayer, LayerAccessChanged)
grep '"type": "sync_event"' merged.jsonl

# Protocol messages (Hello, Welcome, SyncOffer, etc.)
grep '"type": "message_trace"' merged.jsonl

# Layer changes only
grep 'LayerChanged' merged.jsonl

# Dynamic layer creation
grep 'NewDynamicLayer' merged.jsonl

# Events from a specific instance
grep '"instance": "alice"' merged.jsonl

# Pretty-print
cat merged.jsonl | python -m json.tool
```

## Architecture

```
Courier (PeerActor)                    Scribe (Actor)
  │ CourierEvent                         │ PageUpdate
  │ MessageTrace                         │ SyncEvent
  │                                      │
  └─→ serialize to JSON ──┐   ┌── serialize to JSON ←─┘
                           │   │
                    broadcast::Sender<String>
                           │   │
                    ┌──────┴───┴──────┐
                    │  CaptureHandle   │
                    │  (logging_utils) │
                    │                  │
                    │  Subscribes to   │
                    │  all registered  │
                    │  sources         │
                    └────────┬─────────┘
                             │
                     tokio::fs::File
                             │
                      output.jsonl
```

Each crate serializes its own events into pre-serialized JSON strings, keeping `logging_utils` free from courier/scribe type dependencies. The `CaptureHandle` just collects `String` lines from `broadcast::Sender<String>` channels.

### Wiring

| Binary | How capture is wired |
|--------|---------------------|
| **kunki** | `init_rich_tracing_with_capture()` → `CaptureHandle` → registered with Courier + Butler → control server `capture_start`/`capture_end` |
| **sthalam** | `init_rich_tracing_with_capture()` → `CaptureHandle` → broadcast channel registered + set on Butler → passed to `init_p2p()` → Courier gets `capture_tx` → control server `capture_start`/`capture_end` |

## Build

No extra build flags required. The broadcast channels are always compiled in. When no capture is active, `broadcast::send()` with 0 receivers is a no-op (near-zero cost).

## AI Analysis

Feed the merged JSONL file to an AI for debugging sync issues:

```
Here's a capture of a chat sync session between alice (owner),
node, and bob (viewer). Bob can't send messages in a custom channel.
Analyze the event flow and identify where it breaks down.

<attach my_label_merged.jsonl>
```

The AI can trace the full event flow: owner creates channel → node detects dynamic layer → node issues permits → broadcasts to peers → peers receive layer access → messages sync (or don't).

Based on my analysis of the captured JSONL events from the four instances (kunki node, alice, bob, carol), here are the findings:

**3. Are there any AuthorizeLayerSubscriber events?**
NO - No AuthorizeLayerSubscriber events found in any capture file.

**4. Are there NewDynamicLayer / LayerAccessChanged events?**
YES - Found in node capture:
- NewDynamicLayer event for layer path `a05034ce-e743-4b28-84dc-1cecb8b93986/channels/did:key:REDACTED`
- The event includes layer permits for Bob and Carol (with viewer role permissions)

**5. Trace the flow - does Bob write locally → observer fires → broadcast to node?**
NO - The observer fires locally (Bob sees his message in LayerChanged at ts=1770826285), but the write does NOT broadcast to the node.

### The Problem

Bob and Carol's messages appear in:
- Their own local scribe (LayerChanged events showing 2 messages in full_data)
- Alice's cache (Alice receives read_positions updates from Bob and Carol)

But do NOT appear in:
- Node's storage (0/0 matches for "Bob message" and "Carol message" in kunki capture)
- Node's broadcast (only 1 Alice message received by node vs 2 viewer messages that never reach it)

### Message Flow Trace

**Alice's message:**
- LocalWrite -> Observer fires -> Broadcast to node ✓
- Node receives and stores

**Bob's message:**
- LocalWrite -> Observer fires locally ✓
- Broadcast to node ✗ (message bytes never sent)
- Node never receives

**Carol's message:**
- LocalWrite -> Observer fires locally ✓
- Broadcast to node ✗ (message bytes never sent)
- Node never receives

### Root Cause Hypothesis

The issue is in the **Scribe observer subscription broadcast logic** for viewer roles. The observer fires locally (updating the local page state), but the `on_applied` handler or the `Broadcast` channel subscriber may be:

1. Not broadcasting writes from viewers to the node subscriber
2. Filtering out writes from non-owner peers in the broadcast path
3. Not having the node subscribed as a broadcast listener for layers where the observer/writer doesn't have write permissions

The layer permits were issued correctly (NewDynamicLayer event shows Bob and Carol have both `sync: true` and `write: true` in their permits), so the issue is not authorization, but rather the scribe observer not respecting the write flag when deciding what to broadcast.

content.thinking:
Now I have the full picture. Let me look at the permit template:

The viewer permit (issued by node to viewers like Bob) has:
- Fixed layers: `{page_id}/channels/general/messages`, `{page_id}/channels/random/messages`, `{page_id}/channels/dev/messages`, etc.
- `dynamic_layer_schemas`: `channels/{id}/messages` with `grant: "role"` and `role_permissions` for owner, collaborator, node

The dynamic layer schema is `channels/{id}/messages` with role_permissions including `collaborator` with `write: true`.

The node stores the viewer's page permit. When the node checks `Permissions::can_write()`, path 3 loads the stored permit and calls `permit.can_write_layer(layer_name, page_id, peer_did)`.
 
I'm realizing the layer permit is a separate token the node issues for dynamic layers with specific permissions, but looking at the current code, `Permissions::can_write` only checks the subscriber's page permit, sync_target, and the stored page permit—none of which actually validate against the layer permit itself.

The node does have `dynamic_layer_schemas` in its own permit, but `can_write_layer` only checks the `layers` section, not `dynamic_layer_schemas`. So there's a gap: viewers receive layer permits and can read/sync the layer, they write locally in ToSource mode, send a SyncOffer back to the node, but when the node's Scribe calls `Permissions::can_write()`, it's not actually checking the layer permit that was issued.

The viewer's page permit doesn't have the channel layer as a fixed layer, and while the `dynamic_layer_schemas` match, `can_write_layer` doesn't check them, so the write gets rejected. The fix is to make `Permissions::can_write()` on the node check the issued layer permits or `dynamic_layer_schemas` for write access. I should verify whether gurkha's `can_write_layer` already considers `dynamic_layer_schemas` before implementing a fix.

For observability, I'd want to capture write permission decisions with rejection reasons, apply update outcomes with layer names and peer DIDs, and include layer names in message traces so I can correlate the events. But the core issue is clear—the node's permission check rejects Bob's writes because the page permit doesn't cover dynamic layers. Let me add a write permission capture event to confirm this is what's happening.

content.text:
## Observability Gaps: What I Needed But Didn't Have

After spending significant time tracing the captures to find the root cause, here's a comprehensive breakdown.

---

### 1. Write Permission Decisions (`type: "permission_check"`)

**This is the single biggest gap.** The node silently rejected Bob's write to the dynamic layer, and there was **zero trace** of it in the captures. I had to read the source code of `Permissions::can_write()` and mentally simulate all 3 paths to figure out the rejection.

**Where to add:** `scribe/src/permit.rs` — `Permissions::can_write()`

**Fields needed:**
```json
{
  "type": "permission_check",
  "ts": "...",
  "page_id": "pg_123",
  "layer": "channels/did:key:alice.../project-x/messages",
  "peer_did": "did:key:z6MkhL...",
  "operation": "write",
  "result": "denied",
  "path1_subscriber_permit": false,
  "path2_sync_target": false,
  "path3_stored_permit": false,
  "instance": "kunki"
}
```

When result is `"denied"`, include **which paths were tried and why they failed**. When result is `"allowed"`, include **which path granted access**. This would have immediately told me "the node denied Bob's write to the dynamic layer via all 3 paths."

Also add the same for `Permissions::can_local_write()` in `loro_observer.rs` — this catches cases where the local Scribe blocks writes.

---

### 2. Apply Update Outcomes (`type: "apply_update"`)

When `handle_apply_update` completes (success or rejection), there's no capture event. I could only infer rejection from the **absence** of a `page_update` for the dynamic layer on the node — which is error-prone when you're scanning 87 lines.

**Where to add:** `scribe/src/sync/apply.rs` — end of `handle_apply_update()`

**Fields needed:**
```json
{
  "type": "apply_update",
  "ts": "...",
  "page_id": "pg_123",
  "layer": "channels/.../project-x/messages",
  "from_peer": "did:key:z6MkhL...",
  "result": "rejected",
  "reason": "Permission denied: cannot write to layer",
  "created_layer": false,
  "instance": "kunki"
}
```

On success:
```json
{
  "type": "apply_update",
  "ts": "...",
  "page_id": "pg_123",
  "layer": "read_positions",
  "from_peer": "did:key:z6MkhL...",
  "result": "applied",
  "reason": null,
  "created_layer": false,
  "update_size": 142,
  "instance": "kunki"
}
```

---

### 3. Layer Name in Message Traces

The current `message_trace` for SyncOffer/SyncAccept/SyncAck only shows:
```json
{"type": "message_trace", "msg": "SyncOffer", "direction": "Received", "peer_node_id": "dcc3..."}
```

I could see Bob sent SyncOffer and the node sent SyncAccept. But I couldn't tell **which layer** each was for. Bob was syncing both `read_positions` (which worked) and the dynamic layer (which was silently rejected). Without the layer name, I had to correlate timestamps and infer from `page_update` events.

**Where to add:** `courier/src/trace.rs` or wherever message traces are emitted.

**Additional fields:**
```json
{
  "type": "message_trace",
  "msg": "SyncOffer",
  "direction": "Received",
  "peer_node_id": "dcc3...",
  "layer": "channels/.../project-x/messages",
  "update_size": 256,
  "page_id": "pg_123"
}
```

The `layer` and `page_id` fields would let me immediately correlate: "Bob sent SyncOffer for the dynamic layer → node received it → but no apply_update success for that layer → look at permission_check."

---

### 4. Subscriber State Events (`type: "subscriber_state"`)

When the node subscribes Bob, what does the subscriber state look like? What layers is Bob authorized for? Currently I can see individual `layer_auth` events, but there's no snapshot of "here's the full authorization state for this subscriber."

**Where to add:** `scribe/src/sync/subscription.rs` — end of `handle_subscribe()`

**Fields needed:**
```json
{
  "type": "subscriber_state",
  "ts": "...",
  "page_id": "pg_123",
  "action": "subscribed",
  "peer_did": "did:key:z6MkhL...",
  "peer_role": "collaborator",
  "authorized_layers": ["messages", "channels_meta", "presence", "read_positions", "channels/general/messages"],
  "total_layers": 12,
  "can_see_others": true,
  "is_visible": true,
  "instance": "kunki"
}
```

Similarly on unsubscribe. This gives a complete picture at subscription time without having to aggregate individual `layer_auth` events.

---

### 5. Observer Broadcast Decisions (`type: "broadcast_decision"`)

In `loro_observer.rs`, the observer decides per-subscriber whether to broadcast. Currently there's no trace when a subscriber is **skipped** (not in `authorized_dids`). This would have been useful to see "observer fired for dynamic layer, but Bob was not in authorized_dids."

**Where to add:** `scribe/src/loro_observer.rs` — inside the subscriber loop

**Fields needed (only emit on skip, not on success — too noisy):**
```json
{
  "type": "broadcast_decision",
  "ts": "...",
  "page_id": "pg_123",
  "layer": "channels/.../project-x/messages",
  "peer_did": "did:key:z6MkhL...",
  "action": "skipped",
  "reason": "not_in_authorized_dids",
  "instance": "kunki"
}
```

Also emit when skipping due to `is_local_only` or `from_peer` (remote update sender exclusion), but with `reason: "local_only"` or `reason: "sender_exclusion"`.

And in `broadcast_update` (broadcast.rs) and `handle_reconcile_with_peers` (reconcile.rs) — same pattern.

---

### 6. DID-to-Username Mapping Event (`type: "peer_identity"`)

Full DIDs are 50+ characters long. Every time I analyzed events, I had to manually figure out which DID was Alice, Bob, Carol, or the node. A one-time mapping event emitted at connection time would save enormous time.

**Where to add:** `courier/src/peer_actor/mod.rs` — on successful authentication, or in the capture system when capture starts.

```json
{
  "type": "peer_identity",
  "ts": "...",
  "did": "did:key:REDACTED",
  "short_did": "z6MkhL...N22h2s5",
  "username": "bob",
  "node_id": "dcc38caf4e93...",
  "role": "collaborator",
  "instance": "kunki"
}
```

This allows building a lookup table at the start of any analysis session. Would also be useful to add `"peer_name"` or `"short_did"` as a convenience field on ALL events that have a DID, so you don't have to cross-reference.

---

### 7. Convenience Tags on Existing Events

**Add `peer_name` to `layer_auth` events:**

Currently:
```json
{"type": "layer_auth", "action": "authorized", "did": "did:key:REDACTED", ...}
```

Better:
```json
{"type": "layer_auth", "action": "authorized", "did": "did:key:z6Mkn3...", "short_did": "z6Mkn3...dMVG3GT", ...}
```

**Add `layer_short` to all events with a layer name:**

The layer name `channels/did:key:REDACTED` is very long. A shortened version like `channels/.../project-x/messages` or just `project-x/messages` would help scanning.

**Add `event_id` or `seq` for ordering:**

Timestamps have millisecond resolution. Multiple events happen in the same millisecond (e.g., the node emitting 3 `authorized_dynamic_permit` events all at `1770827302323`). A monotonic sequence number per instance would make ordering unambiguous.

**Add `phase` tag for grouping:**

Events naturally cluster into phases. A tag like:
- `"phase": "handshake"` — Hello, Welcome, SyncOffer, SyncAccept during initial connect
- `"phase": "dynamic_layer"` — NewDynamicLayer, LayerPermit, LayerConsent
- `"phase": "steady_state"` — regular SyncOffer/Accept during ongoing operation

This would let you filter `grep '"phase": "dynamic_layer"'` to see just the channel creation flow.

---

### 8. Pending Authorizations State

When `AuthorizeLayerSubscriber` arrives before the layer exists, it goes to `pending_layer_authorizations`. But there's no event showing this. Later when the layer is created and pending authorizations are applied, there is an `applied_pending` event — but if the layer never gets created, the pending authorization silently vanishes.

**Where to add:** `scribe/src/actor.rs` — in the `AuthorizeLayerSubscriber` handler

```json
{
  "type": "layer_auth",
  "action": "stored_pending",
  "layer": "channels/.../project-x/messages",
  "did": "did:key:z6Mkn3...",
  "pending_count": 1,
  "instance": "bob"
}
```

---

### Summary: Priority Order

| Priority | Event | Why |
|----------|-------|-----|
| **P0** | `permission_check` (write denied) | Would have found the root cause in 30 seconds |
| **P0** | `apply_update` (outcome) | Immediately shows rejected updates |
| **P1** | Layer name in `message_trace` | Correlates protocol messages to specific layers |
| **P1** | `peer_identity` mapping | Saves 5 minutes per debugging session |
| **P2** | `subscriber_state` snapshot | Shows full auth picture at subscription time |
| **P2** | `broadcast_decision` (skips) | Shows why data doesn't reach a subscriber |
| **P3** | `short_did` / `layer_short` tags | Readability for manual scanning |
| **P3** | `seq` monotonic counter | Disambiguates same-millisecond events |
| **P3** | `phase` grouping tag | Makes grep filtering more natural |

## Summary

### Root Cause Fix

The node's `Permissions::can_write()` was rejecting writes from viewers (Bob, Carol) to dynamic layers. The dynamic layer path `channels/did:key:alice/project-x/messages` contains Alice's DID, but Bob's page permit only covers layers with Bob's own DID. None of the 3 existing paths in `can_write()` handled this.

**Fix**: Added **path 4** to `Permissions::can_write()` that checks the node's own permit's `dynamic_layer_schemas` against the peer's role. The schema `channels/{id}/messages` has `role_permissions.collaborator.write = true`, so Bob (collaborator) is now authorized.

### Changes

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `gurkha/src/decision/layer.rs` | Added `matches_dynamic_schema_for_role()` + `matches_dynamic_path_any_did()` + 3 tests |
| `gurkha/src/decision/mod.rs` | Export `matches_dynamic_schema_for_role` |
| `gurkha/src/lib.rs` | Re-export `matches_dynamic_schema_for_role` |
| `scribe/src/permit.rs` | Added path 4 to `can_write()` + `get_peer_role()` helper + capture events on each path |
| `scribe/src/state.rs` | Added `emit_permission_check_capture()` + `emit_apply_update_capture()` |
| `scribe/src/sync/apply.rs` | Emit `apply_update` capture on success and rejection |

### New Observability Events

1. **`permission_check`** — emitted for every `can_write()` decision, shows which path granted/denied and why
2. **`apply_update`** — emitted for every `handle_apply_update()` result, shows applied/rejected with reason
